verdict.headline: CONFOUNDED — the 27B does not test synthesis; it tests abstention. Under the strict grounding instruction the 27B abstains 84% on RAG (8B: ~31%), and loses 22:5 (comparison) and 15:1 (temporal) to the 8B on containment. Scale made caution worse, not synthesis better.
verdict.consequence: The synthesis-bottleneck claim as originally framed is NOT causally validated and must be revised: comparison/temporal errors are dominated by abstention on binary verification questions, interacting with a containment metric that cannot credit a cautious non-answer.

benchmark_anatomy.question_form: comparison/temporal questions are META-questions about articles ('do the TechCrunch article and the Hacker News article both report X'), not questions about the world; the natural join key is the ARTICLE, not a world entity

graph_bridging.note: gold doc pairs ARE bridged in the graph (shared entity or edge) 95-100% of the time — connectivity was never the graph's problem

benchmark_anatomy.extraction_quality: the 8B extractor builds metadata triangles — headlines typed as EVENT, outlet domains as LOCATION, dates as EVENT, edges like headline->outlet strength 10 — a CITATION graph, not a knowledge graph; hubs are outlets and dates, which explains both hub domination and why bridges are semantically empty
